input.quote: Each party is responsible for the supervision, direction, and control of its respective personnel. IBM reserves the right to determine the assignment of its personnel.
input.rationale: No non-solicitation, no-hire or inducement restriction binds Customer anywhere in the Agreement. Document-wide searches for "solicit", "hire", "employ", "engage", "induce", "recruit" and "restrictive covenant" return no such provision, and both candidate sections are unrelated: § 14.8 Personnel (p0182) covers only each party's supervision, direction and control of its own personnel, IBM's right to assign its personnel, and IBM's use of Subcontractors and Affiliates; § 14.16 Freedom of Action (p0200) runs in our favour, confirming "Each party is free to enter into similar agreements with others." That satisfies the rule's preferred position ("No non-solicit on Customer"), which is stronger for Bluefly than the mutual 12-month fallback, so this is compliant rather than missing and no redline or counterparty comment is raised — the absence benefits our party and must not be flagged. The deterministic checks for a duration cap of 12 months or less and for a general-solicitation carve-out are non-probative: both presuppose an existing non-solicit clause, and with none in the document there is nothing to measure. Inserting carve-out language would require first importing a restriction on Bluefly that IBM has not sought, worsening our position. Recorded as internal evidence of coverage, not a negotiation issue.
